\title{Exposure Concentration Under a Learned Ranker\\ Is a Cold-Start
       Effect:\\ A Convergence Test in a Simulated Matching Market}

\author{}
\date{}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\noindent
When a recommender decides which candidates a matching market's agents ever
see, what does it do to exposure, and for how long? A finite two-sided market of
1000 agents carries a four-dimensional trait vector and a private commitment
type; a neural collaborative filter produces top-20 shortlists; truncated
deferred acceptance clears the market over those shortlists and nothing else.
Exposure Gini under the learned ranker exceeds an oracle's by $+0.0251$
$[+0.0155, +0.0347]$ over five seeds at a hundred epochs. Extending to three
hundred shows that is not a floor: the gap peaks at $+0.3055$ near the start and
decays to below $0.001$, with a residual that five seeds cannot resolve from
zero, so the hundred-epoch figure is fifty-five times its terminal value. The
ordering is positive in all twelve cells of a parameter sweep, but its size
varies fivefold, and the mechanism --- the filter learning coverage --- fails in
the one cell where coverage never climbs, so convergence is established at one
point and not as a general property. A companion institutional comparison yields
an interior welfare optimum two cells wide. Every parameter is uncalibrated and
five seeds carry every headline.
\end{abstract}
